Optimal.Notes: A 1024x640 render resolution with Deck FSR upscaling to 1280x800 provides a cleaner image than the battery profile while keeping the 30 fps cap stable in most areas. Bump texture and view distance to medium for a noticeably better visual experience without a heavy GPU cost.

profiles.Summary: The First Descendant is a demanding Unreal Engine 5 looter shooter that pushes the Steam Deck hard; 30 fps at low settings with FSR upscaling is the realistic target. The game is listed as Unsupported on Steam Deck and has known anti-cheat concerns that may affect online multiplayer on Linux/Proton.
profiles.BasisNote: No dedicated Steam Deck reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements (GTX 1050 Ti class, matching the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU) and UE5 engine characteristics. On first launch, check frame rate in a busy combat area and drop to the Max Battery profile if it cannot hold 30 fps.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render at 960x600 with Deck FSR upscaling to maximise battery; the 8 W TDP cap and reduced GPU clock will cause occasional dips below 30 fps in dense combat or large open areas. GE-Proton is strongly recommended for better online compatibility.

KnownIssues: Listed as 'Unsupported' by Valve — online and co-op features may be blocked or unstable due to the game's anti-cheat system on Linux/Proton
GameGuard anti-cheat can prevent online play entirely; GE-Proton improves compatibility but is not guaranteed
Heavy UE5 shader compilation stutter on first launch and when entering new areas for the first time
Partial controller support only — some menus and UI elements may require touchscreen or mouse input

MaxPerformance.Notes: Setting the refresh rate to 40 Hz and capping at 40 fps gives the smoothest consistent experience the Deck can realistically sustain; native 1280x800 at full TDP will still dip in heavy boss fights, so drop Effects Quality to Low if frame rate becomes unstable. Battery life will be short at full TDP.

Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz refresh and frame cap deliver a smooth, judder-free feel that feels noticeably better than 30 fps; texture quality bumped to Medium for readable UI and loot text. Expect occasional dips to ~35 fps in crowded multiplayer areas.

profiles.Summary: The First Descendant is a demanding Unreal Engine 5 looter shooter that pushes the Steam Deck to its limits — the minimum GPU spec roughly matches the Deck's RDNA 2, so 30 fps is achievable at low settings with FSR upscaling, but headroom is tight. No Deck-specific reports were found, so all profiles are estimated from PC requirements and hardware class comparisons.
profiles.BasisNote: No Steam Deck or ProtonDB reports were available; all profiles are estimated from the PC minimum requirements (GTX 1050 Ti class GPU — matching the Deck) and UE5 engine behaviour. On first run, check the frame rate in a busy open area or boss fight and drop to the Max Battery profile if it cannot hold your target frame rate.

MaxBattery.Notes: Every setting is at Low with render resolution dropped to 960x600 and the Deck's own FSR doing the upscaling; half-rate shading further reduces GPU load. Even so, dense particle effects during boss fights may cause brief dips below 30 fps.

KnownIssues: Steam Deck is listed as Unsupported; the Easy Anti-Cheat (EAC) implementation may cause launch or online connectivity issues under Proton — try GE-Proton if the default fails.
UE5 Lumen global illumination and Nanite virtualised geometry are extremely GPU-heavy and must be set to their lowest options for any acceptable performance.
The game requires a persistent internet connection and account login, which may add friction on first launch under Proton.
100 GB install size means fast storage is essential; loading times on slower microSD cards may be notably long.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Full TDP with GPU at max clock squeezes out the best frame rate the Deck can realistically sustain; battery life is short so keep a charger nearby. Drop Shadow Quality and Post-Processing back to Low if frame rate falls below 40 fps in busy encounters.
